questions.solution:
For each node, a node with no child contributes 1; otherwise its count comes from its children. Then the count for the right siblings is added.

So only nodes without children (leaves) are counted.

Answer: number of leaf nodes in the tree

questions.text: An instruction pipeline has five stages, namely, instruction fetch (IF), instruction decode and register fetch (ID/RF), instruction execution (Ex), memory access (MEM), and register write back (WB) with stage latencies 1 ns, 2.2 ns, 2 ns, 1 ns, and 0.75 ns, respectively (ns stands for nanoseconds). To gain in terms of frequency, the designers have decided to split the ID/RF stage into three stages (ID, RF1, RF2) each of latency 2.2/3 ns. Also, the Ex stage is split into two stages (Ex1, Ex2) each of latency 1 ns. The new design has a total of eight pipeline stages. A program has 20% branch instructions which execute in the Ex stage and produce the next instruction pointer at the end of the Ex stage in the old design and at the end of the Ex2 stage in the new design. The IF stage stalls after fetching a branch instruction until the next instruction pointer is computed. All instructions other than the branch instruction have an average CPI of one in both the designs. The execution times of this program on the old and the new design are P and Q nanoseconds, respectively. The value of P/Q is __________
questions.solution:
Old design: clock = 2.2 ns. Branch resolved at end of stage 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 stall cycles.
CPI = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 1.4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P = 1.4 [latex]\times[/latex] 2.2 = 3.08 ns per instruction

New design: clock = 1 ns. Branch resolved at end of Ex2 = stage 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 stall cycles.
CPI = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 2 ns per instruction

P/Q = 3.08 / 2 = 1.54

Answer: 1.54

questions.text:
The memory access time is 1 nanosecond for a read operation with a hit in cache, 5
nanoseconds for a read operation with a miss in cache, 2 nanoseconds for a write operation
with a hit in cache and 10 nanoseconds for a write operation with a miss in cache. Execution
of a sequence of instructions involves 100 instruction fetch operations, 60 memory operand
read operations and 40 memory operand write operations. The cache hit-ratio is 0.9. The
average memory access time (in nanoseconds) in executing the sequence of instructions is
__________.
questions.solution:
Reads = 100 fetches + 60 operands = 160, writes = 40.

- Avg read = 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 1.4 ns
- Avg write = 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 2.8 ns

Average = [latex]\frac{160\times1.4+40\times2.8}{200}=\frac{224+112}{200}=1.68[/latex]

Answer: 1.68

questions.text: The above synchronous sequential circuit built using JK flip-flops is initialized with [latex]Q_{2}Q_{1}Q_{0}[/latex] = 000. The state sequence for this circuit for the next 3 clock cycles is
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]J_2=\bar Q_1, K_2=Q_0[/latex]; [latex]J_1=Q_2, K_1=\bar Q_2[/latex]; [latex]J_0=Q_1, K_0=\bar Q_0[/latex].

- 000: J2K2 = 10 (set), J1K1 = 01 (reset), J0K0 = 01 (reset) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 100
- 100: J2K2 = 10, J1K1 = 10 (set), J0K0 = 01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 110
- 110: J2K2 = 00 (hold 1), J1K1 = 10, J0K0 = 11 (toggle) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 111

Answer: 100, 110, 111
